title: Listening: Speaker Attitude
description: Listen to short comments and infer the speaker's real attitude: sarcasm, reluctance, polite refusal and more.

questions.prompt: Listen. How does the speaker feel about the meeting?

media.text: Oh, wonderful. Another three-hour meeting where we decided absolutely nothing. That was the best use of my afternoon.

options.text: Annoyed that it was long and pointless

questions.explanation: "Oh, wonderful" is sarcastic here: three hours and "nothing" decided show frustration.

questions.prompt: Listen. What is the speaker doing?

media.text: Thanks so much for thinking of me. I'd love to, but I've got a lot on my plate this weekend. You guys have fun, though.

questions.explanation: "I'd love to, but" plus a reason and "have fun" is a polite way to refuse.

questions.prompt: Listen. How does the speaker feel about helping?

media.text: Well, I suppose I could stay late and finish the report. If there's really no one else who can do it.

questions.explanation: "I suppose" and "if there's really no one else" show reluctant agreement.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker really think of the soup?

media.text: It's very, um, interesting. I've never tasted anything quite like it. I think I'm actually pretty full already, though.

options.text: They love it and want the recipe
They don't like it but are being polite
They think it's too hot to eat

questions.explanation: Calling food "interesting" and stopping after a few spoonfuls hints at polite dislike.

questions.prompt: Listen. What is the speaker's attitude toward the plan?

media.text: It sounds great in theory. I'm just not sure we can pull it off in two weeks. A lot of things would have to go right.

questions.explanation: "In theory," "I'm just not sure" and "a lot of things have to go right" express doubt.

questions.prompt: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

media.text: Thank goodness the test results came back fine. I've been worried all week. That's a huge weight off my shoulders.

questions.explanation: "Thank goodness" and "weight off my shoulders" express relief after worry.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker imply about Sam?

media.text: Sam said he'd be here at seven sharp. Sam, on time? That'll be the day. Let's order without him.

questions.explanation: "Sam, on time? That'll be the day" means the speaker doesn't expect it, so Sam is often late.

questions.prompt: Listen. How does the speaker feel about the new office?

media.text: The new office is fine, I guess. It's a bit far from the train and the coffee isn't great. But I'll get used to it.

options.text: Planning to quit because of it

questions.explanation: "Fine, I guess" plus small complaints and "I'll get used to it" show mild criticism with acceptance.
